data.narrative:
Astranis, a Series D space and aerospace company founded by John Gedmark and Ryan McLinko, has raised $350M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers (Sierra Space, Apex Space, Varda Space Industries, Skyryse) and five public Space & Aerospace comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression anchors to Astranis's last known post-money valuation of $3.5B, applying a typical 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier to imply $5.2B. The peer-median method references four same-sector comparables with valuations ranging $1.1B to $8.0B, yielding a median of $1.9B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (sector median 26.4x across six tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure. These two methods produce a low estimate of $1.6B, median of $3.6B, and high of $6.0B.

The wide $1.6B–$6.0B range reflects material dispersion within the peer set and uncertainty regarding revenue trajectory. The $3.6B median is supported by both stage-progression logic and peer comparables, though the high end is anchored chiefly to prior fundraising data. Key uncertainties include satellite utilization rates, unit economics on deployed capacity, and competitive positioning within a sector experiencing rapid consolidation.
